turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mrs Whitfield, come on through. How have you been getting on?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Quite well in myself, thank you, doctor. My ankles have been rather troublesome, though.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tell me a bit more about the ankles.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): They swell, particularly by the evening. Um, as to when it started, last winter, or it may have been the winter before. I simply cannot put a date on it.
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I've noticed it when I'm helping her with her shoes. Both sides, and the skin stays dented if you press it.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any shortness of breath with that?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): A little, yes, if I walk up to the shops. Not at rest. I stop and catch my breath, then I am alright.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain at all?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor, none whatsoever.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): And a cough?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): No, I haven't had a cough.
[SEG0012] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She has been more tired in the afternoons, though. She nods off in her chair.
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, I am seventy-eight, and a rest in the afternoon is hardly unusual. But yes, I am more weary than I was.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fair enough. Who's sorting the tablets these days?
[SEG0015] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I am. I live with Mum, and I make up the Webster pack every Sunday. The names are a bit of a muddle, I'll admit.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's alright. Walk me through what she actually swallows.
[SEG0017] person_3 (CAREGIVER): There's the water tablet. That's frusemide, forty milligrams, one in the morning.
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, the water tablet. I have taken that for some time.
[SEG0019] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Then there's the little white one. And, well, actually, I had also written Coversyl down as if it were another tablet, but I think I have counted the same one twice.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Coversyl is only the brand name. What does the blister say?
[SEG0021] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Perindopril, four milligrams, one each morning. The little white one is that. Not two different pills. I doubled it on the list, I'm sorry.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): I have been on that blood pressure tablet for five-ish years, I should think. Perhaps a little longer. I would not swear to it.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Has another doctor stopped anything?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. Dr Lang, at the medical centre, stopped the amlodipine. That was last winter, or possibly the winter before. I cannot be sure which.
[SEG0025] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It was the five milligram one. She has not had it since. Her ankles were already puffy, and he thought that tablet might be making them worse.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right, so no amlodipine now. Any other tablets, or any allergies to medicines?

[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No allergies that I know of. And I do not take anything else, not even from the chemist. We did have a lovely morning tea at the church fete on Saturday, though. The scones were excellent.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm glad the scones were up to scratch. Let me look at your legs and listen to your chest.

[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Both ankles are swollen and they pit. Your lungs are clear, no crackles. Blood pressure is one hundred and fifty-two over eighty-eight, pulse is seventy-four, and your oxygen level is ninety-seven percent.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that blood pressure rather high, doctor?
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): It's a little up, yes. I think this swelling is fluid retention. We'll leave the perindopril as it is. The one I'd like to change is the water tablet.
[SEG0032] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Up or down?
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Up. We'll stop the forty milligrams once a day, and use forty milligrams in the morning and again at lunchtime.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Twice a day. I shall remember. Megan will put it in the pack.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'd also like a blood test for your kidney function and your salts, since we're increasing the frusemide. They can take that this week.
[SEG0036] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I can bring her on Thursday morning, if that suits.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thursday is fine, we'll book it. And come back and see me in a fortnight, so we can check the ankles and look at those bloods.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): A fortnight. Yes, doctor.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): In the meantime, put your feet up when you sit, and ease off the salt. If you become much more breathless, or the swelling climbs up the legs, don't wait, just ring us.
[SEG0040] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'll watch for that. Would it help if I weighed her?
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes. A couple of times a week is plenty. Same scales, in the morning, before breakfast.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor. You have been very clear. I do apologise for not remembering the dates.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not at all. We'll get the Webster pack updated, and I'll see you both in two weeks.
